prompt-development.expert_curated_answer: Nondisjunction is the errors in splitting genetic materials when our body cells divide [17911163]. A type of cell division that takes only one of two copies of each chromosome (cell structures that store genetic information) from the parent cell, for the baby to have a set of chromosomes from each parent, is called meiosis. When the cells divide for growth and to maintain our bodies, the number of chromosomes remains the same in the new cells, and this type of cell division is called mitosis. Non-disjunction can happen during both types of cell division [9557829, 6232200]. When the chromosomes fail to split properly, it causes a condition called aneuploidy (having too many or too few chromosomes instead of the normal two of each)[11283700, 35788750]. Nondisjunction can be caused by the genes and environment [7789361]. During meiosis, both women's eggs and male sperm may have faulty chromosomes. It happens more often in older women [9557829, 35270022] and in men who inherited faulty chromosomes [21311180]. Hormone imbalance plays an important role in nondisjunction [4096700]. Faulty chromosomes in sperm were linked to drug treatments, occupational agents and lifestyle [17292877].
